title: Galatians Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Galatians chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Galatians Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Galatians Chapter 4.

questions.question: In Galatians 4, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The heir is as a child
questions.correctAnswer: The heir is as a child
questions.explanation: This is the first statement made in the chapter, as seen in Galatians 4:1.

questions.question: According to Galatians 4:2, who is the heir under until the time appointed?
questions.correctAnswer: Tutors and governors
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:2 states that the heir is under tutors and governors until the appointed time.

questions.question: What were we in bondage under, as mentioned in Galatians 4:3?
questions.correctAnswer: The elements of the world
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:3 indicates that we were in bondage under the elements of the world.

questions.question: Who did God send forth when the fullness of the time was come, according to Galatians 4:4?
questions.correctAnswer: His Son
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:4 states that God sent forth his Son.

questions.question: What was the purpose of sending His Son, as stated in Galatians 4:5?
options: To redeem them that were under the law
questions.correctAnswer: To redeem them that were under the law
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:5 indicates that the purpose was to redeem those under the law.

questions.question: What has God sent into our hearts, according to Galatians 4:6?
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit of his Son
questions.explanation: In Galatians 4:6, it is stated that God has sent forth the Spirit of his Son into our hearts.

questions.question: According to Galatians 4:7, what are we if we are sons?
questions.correctAnswer: Heirs of God
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:7 clearly states that if we are sons, then we are heirs of God through Christ.

questions.question: What did ye do when ye knew not God, as mentioned in Galatians 4:8?
options: Did service unto them which are no gods
questions.correctAnswer: Did service unto them which are no gods
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:8 mentions that when we did not know God, we served those which by nature are no gods.

questions.question: What is Paul concerned about in Galatians 4:11?
questions.correctAnswer: He has labored in vain
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:11 shows Paul's concern that he has bestowed labor upon them in vain.

questions.question: In Galatians 4:10, what do the people observe?
questions.correctAnswer: Days, months, and years
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:10 specifically mentions observing days, months, times, and years.

questions.question: According to Galatians 4:4, who was made under the law?
questions.correctAnswer: The Son
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:4 states that the Son was made under the law.

questions.question: True or False: Galatians 4:6 mentions that we cry out, 'Abba, Father'.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:6 states that the Spirit of his Son cries, 'Abba, Father'.

questions.question: True or False: In Galatians 4:3, Paul refers to us as free men.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:3 talks about being in bondage, implying we were not free men.

questions.question: True or False: Galatians 4:5 states that we might receive the adoption of children.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:5 states we might receive the adoption of sons, not children.

questions.question: True or False: Galatians 4:9 talks about returning to weak and beggarly elements.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:9 asks how they could turn again to the weak and beggarly elements.

medium.title: Galatians Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Galatians Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: In Galatians 4:14, how did the Galatians receive Paul despite his physical infirmity?
options: As an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: As an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:14 states that the Galatians did not despise or reject Paul's temptation in the flesh but received him as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.

questions.question: What does Galatians 4:16 promise will happen if Paul tells the truth, as commanded in Galatians 4:15?
options: They will pluck out their eyes for him
questions.correctAnswer: Paul becomes their enemy
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:16 asks if Paul has become their enemy because he tells them the truth, connecting to 4:15 where Paul speaks of their previous blessedness and willingness to sacrifice for him.

questions.question: According to Galatians 4:19, what is Paul's spiritual condition in relation to the Galatians?
options: He is travailing in birth until Christ be formed in them
He is indifferent about their faith
He is rejoicing over their progress
He is angry with their disobedience
questions.correctAnswer: He is travailing in birth until Christ be formed in them
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:19 describes Paul as travailing in birth again for the Galatians until Christ is formed in them, indicating his deep spiritual concern.

questions.question: How do Galatians 4:17 and 4:18 contrast the motives of others affecting the Galatians?
options: Some affect them zealously for selfish reasons, but good zeal is always commendable
All zeal is bad and should be avoided
No one affects the Galatians zealously
Zeal is irrelevant to Christian living
questions.correctAnswer: Some affect them zealously for selfish reasons, but good zeal is always commendable
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:17 speaks of those who zealously affect the Galatians but not well, desiring to exclude them, whereas 4:18 notes it is good to be zealously affected always in a good thing.

questions.question: What practical lesson about honesty can be drawn from Galatians 4:16?
options: Telling the truth may cause others to view you as an enemy
Avoid telling the truth to keep peace
Truth is optional in Christian relationships
questions.correctAnswer: Telling the truth may cause others to view you as an enemy
questions.explanation: In Galatians 4:16, Paul asks if he has become an enemy because he tells the truth, showing that honesty can lead to opposition.

questions.question: According to Galatians 4:12, how does Paul urge the Galatians to be?
options: As he is, for he is as they are
questions.correctAnswer: As he is, for he is as they are
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:12 records Paul beseeching the brethren to be as he is, emphasizing his equality with them and their unity.

questions.question: What does Paul express about his relationship with the Galatians in Galatians 4:15?
options: They would have plucked out their own eyes and given them to him if possible
questions.correctAnswer: They would have plucked out their own eyes and given them to him if possible
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:15 states that Paul bears witness that the Galatians spoke of blessedness and would have given their own eyes to him if possible.

questions.question: How does Paul describe those who zealously affect the Galatians in Galatians 4:17?
options: They affect them not well and want to exclude the Galatians
They have pure motives and love
They are indifferent to the Galatians
questions.correctAnswer: They affect them not well and want to exclude the Galatians
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:17 explains that some zealously affect the Galatians but not well, desiring to exclude them so that they themselves might be affected.

questions.question: What is Paul's emotional state in Galatians 4:20 regarding the Galatians?
options: He stands in doubt about them
He is fully confident in them
questions.correctAnswer: He stands in doubt about them
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:20 reveals Paul's desire to be with the Galatians and to change his voice because he stands in doubt about them, showing concern.

questions.question: What spiritual analogy does Paul use in Galatians 4:22 to illustrate two different covenants?
options: Abraham's two sons, one by a bondmaid and one by a freewoman
Moses and Aaron as two leaders
questions.correctAnswer: Abraham's two sons, one by a bondmaid and one by a freewoman
questions.explanation: In Galatians 4:22, Paul refers to Abraham having two sons, one by a bondmaid and another by a freewoman, as an allegory for two covenants.

questions.question: According to Galatians 4:13, what was Paul's condition when he first preached the gospel to the Galatians?
questions.correctAnswer: Infirmity of the flesh
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:13 states that Paul preached the gospel to the Galatians through infirmity of the flesh at the first.

questions.question: What does Paul imply about observing days, months, times, and years in Galatians 4:10?
options: It is a sign of faith
questions.correctAnswer: It is returning to bondage
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:9-10 connects the observation of days, months, times, and years to a desire to be in bondage again, after knowing God.

questions.question: True or False: In Galatians 4:6, the Spirit of God's Son cries, 'Abba, Father' in the hearts of believers.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:6 clearly states that God has sent forth the Spirit of his Son into believers' hearts, crying, 'Abba, Father.'

questions.question: True or False: According to Galatians 4:9, after knowing God, the Galatians are encouraged to return to the weak and beggarly elements for spiritual growth.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:9 warns against turning again to the weak and beggarly elements after knowing God, implying this is a negative regression.

questions.question: True or False: Galatians 4:11 expresses Paul's confidence that his labor with the Galatians was never in vain.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:11 expresses Paul's fear that his labor might have been in vain, showing concern, not confidence.

hard.title: Galatians Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Galatians Chapter 4.

questions.question: According to Galatians 4:23, who was born after the flesh?
options: He who was of the bondwoman
questions.correctAnswer: He who was of the bondwoman
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:23 states, 'But he who was of the bondwoman was born after the flesh;' indicating that the son of the bondwoman was born according to the flesh.

questions.question: What does the allegory in Galatians 4:24 represent?
options: The two covenants: one from Mount Sinai and the other from the promise
The two sons of Abraham: Isaac and Ishmael
The difference between law and grace
The contrast between freedom and slavery in Rome
questions.correctAnswer: The two covenants: one from Mount Sinai and the other from the promise
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:24 explains that these things are an allegory representing 'the two covenants; the one from the mount Sinai, which gendereth to bondage, which is Agar.'

questions.question: In Galatians 4:25, what is Agar identified as?
questions.correctAnswer: Mount Sinai in Arabia
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:25 states, 'For this Agar is mount Sinai in Arabia,' identifying Agar with Mount Sinai in Arabia.

questions.question: What does Galatians 4:26 say Jerusalem above is?
options: Free, which is the mother of us all
The place of the old covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Free, which is the mother of us all
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:26 says, 'But Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all.'

questions.question: According to Galatians 4:28, who are the children of promise?
questions.correctAnswer: We, brethren, as Isaac was
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:28 states, 'Now we, brethren, as Isaac was, are the children of promise.'

questions.question: What instruction does Galatians 4:30 give regarding the bondwoman and her son?
options: Cast out the bondwoman and her son
Embrace the bondwoman and her son
Honor the bondwoman and her son
Protect the bondwoman and her son
questions.correctAnswer: Cast out the bondwoman and her son
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:30 says, 'Cast out the bondwoman and her son: for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the freewoman.'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'allegory' (Galatians 4:24) mean?
options: A symbolic narrative conveying a deeper spiritual meaning
questions.correctAnswer: A symbolic narrative conveying a deeper spiritual meaning
questions.explanation: In Galatians 4:24, 'allegory' refers to a symbolic narrative used by Paul to represent two covenants, conveying a deeper spiritual meaning beyond the literal sense.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Galatians 4:22-31?
questions.correctAnswer: Allegory
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:22-31 uses allegory to compare the two women and their sons to two covenants, illustrating spiritual truths through symbolic narrative (Galatians 4:24).

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is connected to the allegory of the two women in Galatians 4:22-31?
questions.correctAnswer: Genesis 16 and 21
questions.explanation: The allegory in Galatians 4:22-31 refers to Abraham's two sons, one by the bondwoman Hagar and one by the freewoman Sarah, events found in Genesis chapters 16 and 21.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage does Galatians 4:4-5 fulfill by explaining the sending of the Son 'made under the law'?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 8:3
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:4-5 says God sent His Son 'made under the law' to redeem those under the law, which is echoed and expanded in Romans 8:3 discussing God sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh to condemn sin.

questions.question: What precedes Galatians 4:23 in the text?
options: Paul quoting the law about Abraham's two sons
Paul discussing the adoption of sons
Paul exhorting to be as he is
Paul mentioning the Spirit crying 'Abba, Father'
questions.correctAnswer: Paul quoting the law about Abraham's two sons
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:22 immediately precedes 4:23 and contains the statement, 'For it is written, that Abraham had two sons, the one by a bondmaid, the other by a freewoman,' preparing the allegory in 4:23.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'Jerusalem which now is' in Galatians 4:25?
options: It represents the present earthly Jerusalem in bondage
It refers to the heavenly Jerusalem
It symbolizes the new covenant freedom
It is a prophetic vision of the future Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: It represents the present earthly Jerusalem in bondage
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:25 states, 'answereth to Jerusalem which now is, and is in bondage with her children,' indicating the present earthly Jerusalem under bondage.

questions.question: How does the persecution described in Galatians 4:29 relate to the spiritual conflict in the early church?
options: It parallels Ishmael persecuting Isaac, symbolizing conflict between law and Spirit
It refers to Roman persecution of Christians
It describes Jewish rejection of the gospel
It represents internal disputes among the Galatians
questions.correctAnswer: It parallels Ishmael persecuting Isaac, symbolizing conflict between law and Spirit
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:29 says, 'as then he that was born after the flesh persecuted him that was born after the Spirit,' paralleling Ishmael's persecution of Isaac, symbolizing the conflict between the law and the Spirit.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Greek word 'heir' as used in Galatians 4:7?
options: A person entitled to inherit property or status
A slave bound to a master
questions.correctAnswer: A person entitled to inherit property or status
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:7 says, 'if a son, then an heir of God through Christ,' meaning a person entitled to inherit God's promises and status, not a servant or slave.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the allegory of the two women in Galatians 4:22-31?
options: To contrast the covenant of law and the covenant of promise
To illustrate the genealogy of Abraham
To describe historical events in Arabia
To teach about marriage customs in the first century
questions.correctAnswer: To contrast the covenant of law and the covenant of promise
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:22-31 uses the allegory of the two women to represent two covenants: one from Mount Sinai leading to bondage (law), and one of promise leading to freedom.

theological.title: Galatians Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Galatians Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Galatians 4:5 teach about salvation?
options: Redemption from the law to receive sonship adoption
Justification by works of the law
questions.correctAnswer: Redemption from the law to receive sonship adoption
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:5 states that Christ was sent to redeem those under the law so that they might receive the adoption of sons, teaching salvation as redemption leading to divine sonship.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin is taught in Galatians 4:3?
options: Humanity was once in bondage under elemental spiritual forces
Original sin is only a symbolic concept
Sin is overcome by human effort alone
There is no bondage before faith
questions.correctAnswer: Humanity was once in bondage under elemental spiritual forces
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:3 explains that when we were children, we were in bondage under the elements of the world, indicating the doctrine of human bondage to sin and spiritual elements before Christ.

questions.question: What doctrine does Galatians 4:7 teach about our relationship to God after salvation?
options: Believers are no longer servants but sons and heirs through Christ
Salvation leads to a neutral standing with God
Inheritance is based on law observance
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are no longer servants but sons and heirs through Christ
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:7 states that believers are no longer servants but sons, and if sons, then heirs of God through Christ, teaching sonship and inheritance as central to salvation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Galatians 4:6 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Immanence
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:6 shows God's immanence by sending the Spirit of His Son into believers' hearts, illustrating God's nearness and active presence in believers.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily revealed in Galatians 4:4?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:4 shows God's sovereignty in sending His Son at the appointed time, demonstrating His control over redemptive history.

questions.question: How does Galatians 4:22-31 connect to the broader biblical narrative?
options: It allegorizes the two covenants, fulfilling the promise to Abraham
It calls believers back to Mosaic law for salvation
It rejects the Old Testament covenant entirely
It introduces a new covenant unrelated to the past
questions.correctAnswer: It allegorizes the two covenants, fulfilling the promise to Abraham
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:22-31 uses the story of Abraham’s two sons as an allegory to explain the two covenants, connecting to the Abrahamic promise and fulfillment in Christ.

questions.question: In what way does Galatians 4:8-9 prepare for New Testament teaching on idolatry and freedom?
options: By contrasting former bondage to idols with knowledge of the true God
By encouraging ritual observance to avoid idolatry
By teaching that pagan gods are actually divine
By denying any past spiritual bondage
questions.correctAnswer: By contrasting former bondage to idols with knowledge of the true God
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:8-9 contrasts previous service to false gods with knowing God, preparing the New Testament theme of freedom from idolatry through Christ.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Galatians 4:1 and 4:7 teach about sonship and inheritance?
options: Though heirs are children under guardianship, believers become sons and heirs through Christ
Heirs remain servants even after coming of age
Sonship is a metaphor without legal significance
questions.correctAnswer: Though heirs are children under guardianship, believers become sons and heirs through Christ
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:1 explains heirs as children under guardianship, and 4:7 shows that believers become sons and heirs through Christ, teaching progression from guardianship to full inheritance.

questions.question: What doctrine about spiritual bondage and freedom is taught by Galatians 4:3 and 4:31?
options: Believers move from bondage under elemental spirits to freedom as children of the free woman
Bondage is eternal with no hope for freedom
Bondage is only physical and not spiritual
questions.correctAnswer: Believers move from bondage under elemental spirits to freedom as children of the free woman
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:3 describes bondage under the elements of the world, while 4:31 contrasts children of the bondwoman (bondage) with children of the freewoman (freedom), teaching liberation in Christ.

questions.question: What theological synthesis do Galatians 4:19 and 4:20 provide concerning sanctification?
options: Paul’s spiritual labor until Christ is formed in believers expresses ongoing sanctification
Sanctification is instantaneous and complete at conversion
Sanctification depends on observing feast days
Paul doubts the possibility of sanctification
questions.correctAnswer: Paul’s spiritual labor until Christ is formed in believers expresses ongoing sanctification
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:19 shows Paul’s travail until Christ is formed in believers, and 4:20 expresses concern for their spiritual state, teaching sanctification as a progressive formation in Christ.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Galatians 4:10-11 teaches that observing days and times is essential for salvation. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Paul fears their regression to legalistic observance, implying such observance is not salvific
It commands strict observance of festivals for salvation
It teaches that salvation is through works of the law
It endorses pagan festivals as Christian practice
questions.correctAnswer: Paul fears their regression to legalistic observance, implying such observance is not salvific
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:10-11 shows Paul’s concern that the Galatians are returning to observing days and times, which he fears means labor in vain, implying such observance is not the basis of salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine about the incarnation is taught in Galatians 4:4?
options: The Son was made of a woman and made under the law to fulfill redemptive history
The Son was only a divine apparition without human nature
The incarnation was unnecessary for salvation
Jesus was born outside the law
questions.correctAnswer: The Son was made of a woman and made under the law to fulfill redemptive history
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:4 states Christ was born of a woman and made under the law, teaching the incarnation as fully human and fulfilling the law’s requirements in redemption.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially evident in Galatians 4:17?
questions.correctAnswer: Deceptive Wisdom
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:17 describes others zealously affecting the Galatians but not well, aiming to exclude Paul, revealing a misuse of wisdom and zeal in opposition to true teaching.

questions.question: What theological insight does Galatians 4:26 provide in the context of the allegory of the two Jerusalems?
options: The heavenly Jerusalem is free and is the mother of believers, contrasting earthly bondage
The earthly Jerusalem is the ultimate hope for salvation
Both Jerusalems are equally under the law
The allegory rejects any heavenly reality
questions.correctAnswer: The heavenly Jerusalem is free and is the mother of believers, contrasting earthly bondage
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:26 states that Jerusalem above is free and the mother of us all, contrasting with the current Jerusalem in bondage and teaching believers’ citizenship in the heavenly city.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about spiritual adoption and divine knowledge is taught in Galatians 4:6 and 4:9?
options: The Spirit confirms believers as sons who know God personally, not returning to bondage
Knowledge of God is irrelevant to adoption
Adoption is automatic without the Spirit
Return to legalism is encouraged after adoption
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit confirms believers as sons who know God personally, not returning to bondage
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:6 shows the Spirit sent into hearts crying Abba, confirming sonship, while 4:9 warns against returning to weak elements, highlighting the personal knowledge and freedom of adopted sons.
